bull_bear.body:
- India's only end-to-end integrated dental products company - laboratory offerings, clear aligners, aligner materials and equipment, intraoral scanners and paediatric products on a single platform, supporting quality control, process efficiency and cross-selling
- Second-largest player in the domestic dental laboratory business and the largest export dental laboratory; amongst the top two largest dental laboratories in India by revenue for Fiscal 2026
- Backward integration through Taglus into thermoforming sheets, biocompatible 3D-printing resins and thermoforming machines manufactured in-house, giving control over materials and manufacturing processes
- Large Dental Network of over 22,000 clinics, dental companies and dentists across 320+ cities that strengthens brand visibility, aids customer acquisition and enables cross-selling
- Preferred partner to one of the largest Dental Service Organisations in the USA, with more than 1,900 clinics, providing headroom for expansion
- Diversified branded portfolio - Illusion Zirconia, Illusion Aligners, Taglus and Kids-e-Dental; Illusion Aligners was the first Indian aligner brand to receive US FDA 510(k) clearance
- Technology-led capabilities integrating scanners, 3D printing, CNC equipment and software, supported by quality systems and regulatory compliance that provide access to regulated geographies
- Experienced management team - promoters and professionals with significant experience across dentistry, manufacturing, finance and international business
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on the Dental Network — Business growth depends on the continued onboarding, engagement and retention of dental partners - the 22,000+ clinics, dental companies and dentists are the route to market for every product line, so attrition or disengagement directly constrains growth. Mitigation is continued investment in sales and marketing and deeper digital penetration to increase wallet share.
- Manufacturing concentration in and around Mumbai — Six manufacturing and five supporting facilities are heavily concentrated in Mira Road, Mumbai and Boisar, exposing operations to location-specific disruption. Mitigation is disaster-recovery planning and evaluating geographical diversification over time.
- Regulatory and quality compliance across multiple jurisdictions — The Company must comply with Indian and international regulatory and quality standards including US FDA, ISO and CDSCO requirements, plus EU Regulation 2017/745. Loss or lapse of a licence or certification would cut off access to regulated export geographies. Mitigation is qualified regulatory advisers, timely licence renewal and maintenance of ISO and US FDA certifications.
- Supply chain dependence and pricing pressure — Dependence on raw materials combined with the absence of long-term customer orders exposes the Company to supply disruption and price fluctuation, with no contracted volume to absorb it. Mitigation is a diversified vendor base and limiting concentration among related-party suppliers.
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure — The Company operates in a competitive industry characterised by pricing pressure and multiple market participants. Mitigation is differentiated services and solutions, stronger dentist relationships and loyalty, and continued brand-building investment.
- Financial risk - liquidity, interest rate, customer credit and contingent liabilities — Exposure arises from liquidity requirements, interest-rate movements, customer credit and contingent liabilities. Mitigation is adequate liquidity, an appropriate mix of fixed- and floating-rate borrowings, regular review of customer creditworthiness, an Expected Credit Loss provisioning matrix and a prudent approach to contingent liabilities.
- Export and geographic concentration, including US tariff exposure — A large share of revenue comes from outside India (USA 19.36%, UK 10.10%, others 6.10% of the geographic revenue mix), and the international laboratory business is the faster-growing half. Management explicitly cites higher US tariffs and the geopolitical situation as having affected reported profitability in 2025-26 and as a temporary headwind to the international laboratory business.
- Customer concentration in the US channel — The Company describes itself as the preferred partner for one of the largest Dental Service Organisations in the USA with more than 1,900 clinics. That relationship is presented as a growth advantage, but it also concentrates a material part of the US export business in a single counterparty relationship.

- Described (per the F&S Report) as 'India's only end to end integrated dental products company', with a comparison grid showing it as the sole company covering custom-made fixed prosthesis, removable prosthesis, clear aligners, aligner sheet, thermo-forming machine, intraoral scanner and paediatric crowns.

- B2B2C direct-connect model with 22,000+ dental clinics, dental companies and dentists across 320+ cities and 95+ countries; deck argues successful global aligner companies are doctor-led/B2B2C while D2C models 'have struggled to establish in the market'.

- [Listing/history] Journey began in 1989 with a small dental lab; incorporated July 2004 as 'Laxmi Dental Export Private Limited'; listed on Indian stock exchanges on January 20, 2025.

business.body: Laxmi Dental manufactures fully customised, patient-specific dental prostheses (crowns, bridges, abutments, dentures, zirconia and porcelain-fused-to-metal restorations) to dentists' prescriptions for the Indian market and for the USA, UK and Europe. It also makes dentist-prescribed clear aligners under Illusion Aligners on a B2B2C model, is backward integrated through Taglus into aligner sheets, biocompatible 3D-printing resins and thermoforming machines, and sells paediatric dental products through the Kids-e-Dental LLP jointly controlled entity. A digital layer of iScanPro intraoral scanners and the iScope 360 remote dental platform connects dentists to its laboratories.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue investing in innovation, expanding digital adoption, strengthening manufacturing capabilities and growing presence across domestic and international markets
- Drive digital adoption via scanner deployment - every scanner deployed strengthens the connection with clinicians, enhances workflow efficiency and creates recurring opportunities across the laboratory, aligners and digital solutions businesses; digital penetration in the domestic laboratory is targeted to exceed 90% over the medium term from around 75% in 2025-26
- Build an AI and digital ecosystem - investment in AI Dent (IDBG AI Dent Global Private Limited, a 49% joint venture acquired 18 September, 2025) and the launch of iScope 360, an AI-connected remote dental platform for remote oral scanning, treatment monitoring and virtual consultation
- Widen the aligner portfolio beyond conventional orthodontics - Teen Aligners and Personalised Early Orthodontic Treatment (PEOT) added during 2025-26 to serve orthodontists, general dentists and paediatric dentists and create cross-selling across the Dental Network
- Leverage the integrated, vertically integrated model where each business complements the other, with backward integration through Taglus into aligner materials, resins and thermoforming machines
- Deepen the Dental Network of 22,000+ clinics, dental companies and dentists as a source of clinical insight, cross-selling and wallet share, supported by brand-building (including IPL advertising and celebrity-led communication) and dentist/KOL education programmes
- Expand international business through Dental Service Organisations, clinic chains, large dental laboratories and distributor-led expansion for Taglus, supported by participation in international dental events
- Rationalise lower-margin activities within the Other Business category (dental distribution products, dental clinical services and dental education)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Laxmi Dental manufactures across six manufacturing facilities and five supporting facilities spread over more than 1,47,000 square feet as of 31 March, 2026 - three at Mira Road (Maharashtra), two in Mumbai, one in Delhi, one in Bengaluru, one in Ahmedabad, two in Boisar (Maharashtra) and one in Kochi (Kerala), plus a SEEPZ laboratory operating as a 100% export-oriented unit. The Company describes no new plant or commissioning project in the routed narrative chapters; expansion in 2025-26 was instead portfolio, network and technology led: the Illusion Aligners portfolio was widened with Teen Aligners and Personalised Early Orthodontic Treatment, iScope 360 (an AI-connected remote dental platform) was introduced for dental professionals in India while international opportunities were being evaluated, and 1,009 intraoral scanners were sold during the year as digital penetration rose to about 75% in both the domestic and international laboratory businesses. Inorganically, the Company acquired a 49% stake in IDBG AI Dent Global Private Limited on 18 September, 2025, which became a joint venture during the year and supports its AI dental imaging and X-ray analysis development pipeline. Management states it will continue strengthening manufacturing capabilities, and cites geographical diversification of manufacturing as a mitigation it will evaluate over time given the concentration of facilities in and around Mumbai. Separately, the Notice of the 22nd AGM (routed into the governance bundle of this same annual report rather than this one) puts to shareholders a special resolution to vary the objects of the IPO proceeds and extend the utilisation timeline: the machinery-capex objects for the Company and for subsidiary Bizdent Devices Private Limited were only partly spent (40.87% and 10.51% respectively), with the unutilised funds proposed to be reallocated to a newly added object.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Digital adoption is described as one of the strongest structural trends shaping dentistry, and the Company says it continues to invest ahead of this curve
- Domestic laboratory business grew 10.20% and the international laboratory business expanded 29.15% in 2025-26, which management attributes to increasing digital adoption, stronger clinician engagement and growing acceptance across global markets despite temporary tariff-related headwinds
- Scanner sales grew 85.91% during the year as more clinicians embraced digital workflows; 1,009 intraoral scanners were sold in 2025-26
- Aligners delivered steady growth of 7.02%, reflecting category resilience and differentiated offerings
- Reported profitability was affected by higher US tariffs, increased non-cash ESOP expenses and a one-time gratuity past-service liability arising from changes in the labour codes
- Industry outlook is described as favourable, supported by growing prevalence of oral diseases, rising awareness of preventive care, higher demand for aesthetic treatments and continued adoption of digitally enabled solutions; affordability, limited insurance coverage and uneven access to specialised care remain constraints
- Organised participants offering quality products, broad treatment solutions, regulatory compliance and digitally integrated services are expected to be better positioned to address the evolving market opportunity
- Changing regulatory requirements in medical devices are expected to transition the fragmented and unorganised Indian dental products market to an organised and consolidated market dominated by companies focused on quality, operational efficiency and consumer experience
- Laboratories with scalable production, skilled technicians, strong quality systems and digitally integrated workflows are expected to be better positioned; equipment cost may constrain adoption among smaller laboratories

deepdive.thesis: Laxmi Dental delivered a strong Q4FY26 recovery with record revenue (INR 74cr, +22% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins (18.3%) despite US tariff headwinds, driven by robust international lab growth (+40.9%) and strategic scanner deployment. The launch of iScope 360 and normalization of US tariffs to 10% position the company for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion in FY27.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Laxmi Dental manufactures fully customised, patient-specific dental prostheses (crowns, bridges, abutments, dentures, zirconia and porcelain-fused-to-metal restorations) to dentists' prescriptions for the Indian market and for the USA, UK and Europe. It also makes dentist-prescribed clear aligners under Illusion Aligners on a B2B2C model, is backward integrated through Taglus into aligner sheets, biocompatible 3D-printing resins and thermoforming machines, and sells paediatric dental products through the Kids-e-Dental LLP jointly controlled entity. A digital layer of iScanPro intraoral scanners and the iScope 360 remote dental platform connects dentists to its laboratories.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Digital adoption is described as one of the strongest structural trends shaping dentistry, and the Company says it continues to invest ahead of this curve
- Domestic laboratory business grew 10.20% and the international laboratory business expanded 29.15% in 2025-26, which management attributes to increasing digital adoption, stronger clinician engagement and growing acceptance across global markets despite temporary tariff-related headwinds
- Scanner sales grew 85.91% during the year as more clinicians embraced digital workflows; 1,009 intraoral scanners were sold in 2025-26
- Aligners delivered steady growth of 7.02%, reflecting category resilience and differentiated offerings
- Reported profitability was affected by higher US tariffs, increased non-cash ESOP expenses and a one-time gratuity past-service liability arising from changes in the labour codes
- Industry outlook is described as favourable, supported by growing prevalence of oral diseases, rising awareness of preventive care, higher demand for aesthetic treatments and continued adoption of digitally enabled solutions; affordability, limited insurance coverage and uneven access to specialised care remain constraints
- Organised participants offering quality products, broad treatment solutions, regulatory compliance and digitally integrated services are expected to be better positioned to address the evolving market opportunity
- Changing regulatory requirements in medical devices are expected to transition the fragmented and unorganised Indian dental products market to an organised and consolidated market dominated by companies focused on quality, operational efficiency and consumer experience
- Laboratories with scalable production, skilled technicians, strong quality systems and digitally integrated workflows are expected to be better positioned; equipment cost may constrain adoption among smaller laboratories

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Laxmi Dental manufactures across six manufacturing facilities and five supporting facilities spread over more than 1,47,000 square feet as of 31 March, 2026 - three at Mira Road (Maharashtra), two in Mumbai, one in Delhi, one in Bengaluru, one in Ahmedabad, two in Boisar (Maharashtra) and one in Kochi (Kerala), plus a SEEPZ laboratory operating as a 100% export-oriented unit. The Company describes no new plant or commissioning project in the routed narrative chapters; expansion in 2025-26 was instead portfolio, network and technology led: the Illusion Aligners portfolio was widened with Teen Aligners and Personalised Early Orthodontic Treatment, iScope 360 (an AI-connected remote dental platform) was introduced for dental professionals in India while international opportunities were being evaluated, and 1,009 intraoral scanners were sold during the year as digital penetration rose to about 75% in both the domestic and international laboratory businesses. Inorganically, the Company acquired a 49% stake in IDBG AI Dent Global Private Limited on 18 September, 2025, which became a joint venture during the year and supports its AI dental imaging and X-ray analysis development pipeline. Management states it will continue strengthening manufacturing capabilities, and cites geographical diversification of manufacturing as a mitigation it will evaluate over time given the concentration of facilities in and around Mumbai. Separately, the Notice of the 22nd AGM (routed into the governance bundle of this same annual report rather than this one) puts to shareholders a special resolution to vary the objects of the IPO proceeds and extend the utilisation timeline: the machinery-capex objects for the Company and for subsidiary Bizdent Devices Private Limited were only partly spent (40.87% and 10.51% respectively), with the unutilised funds proposed to be reallocated to a newly added object.
